propositions: Task and story that are direct children of the same epic cannot hold a direct dependency link because type-tier promotion escalates the task to epic level, recording an epic-blocks-child edge instead of the intended task-story edge.

Blocking link comparability should be determined by structural position in the parent hierarchy (nearest common ancestor), not by ticket type tier, so cross-subtree dependencies escalate to NCA children rather than type-matched tiers.

Redundancy validation occurs on the original endpoint pair before promotion, missing cases where the promoted pair becomes ancestor-descendant; it must be recomputed from the resolved endpoints for blocking relations only.

Ancestor walk is capped at max_hops=2, truncating chains deeper than epic-story-task and causing fallback to chain root; removing the cap and guarding against cycles allows correct escalation to NCA for deep hierarchies.

Three existing resolver test cases change under structural comparability: cross-story and cross-epic cousins now escalate to their parents and grandparent respectively, with was_redirected=true, inverting the current type-tier behavior.
